header.title: Debt snowball vs avalanche calculator
header.intro: See how long it could take to become debt-free, and how much interest you could pay, if you put every extra dollar toward your smallest balance (snowball) or your highest APR (avalanche). Figures are illustrative estimates, not a promise of savings.

demoBanner.strong: Illustrative only — not a payoff plan or a guarantee.
demoBanner.body: This comparison uses the balances, rates, and payments you enter. Real due dates, fees, and rate changes are not modeled. Nothing here is an offer, advice, or a claim about any program.

results.growingWarning: At least one minimum is below that debt’s monthly interest, so that balance will grow until it is the focus of the extra payment.
results.cappedWarning: The estimate reached the {{years}}-year cap without paying the debts off.
results.summaryMessage: Snowball pays the smallest starting balance first; avalanche pays the highest APR first. Freed minimums roll to the next debt. Estimates assume a constant APR and that you pay on time every month. They are not a payoff plan, a loan offer, or a guarantee of savings or timing.
results.tipAvalanche: Avalanche usually costs less interest because more of each extra dollar goes to the most expensive debt first. Snowball pays off a smaller account sooner, which some people find easier to stick with. The better fit depends on what you can sustain — this is not a recommendation.
results.tipSame: With these numbers, both methods produce the same payoff time and interest. Try changing a balance, APR, or the extra payment to see them diverge.
results.tipNever: If a minimum does not cover interest, that balance grows until extra payments are applied to it. Raising the extra payment or the minimum can change the picture. This is an estimate, not advice.
results.cappedTime: Would not pay off in {{years}} yrs

snowball.title: Debt snowball calculator
snowball.intro: The snowball method puts every extra dollar toward your smallest balance first, then rolls that payment onto the next-smallest. This page starts there — switch to Compare or Avalanche anytime. Figures are illustrative estimates, not a promise of savings.

avalanche.title: Debt avalanche calculator
avalanche.intro: The avalanche method puts every extra dollar toward your highest APR first, then rolls that payment onto the next-highest. This page starts there — switch to Compare or Snowball anytime. Figures are illustrative estimates, not a promise of savings.
